name: SET domain containing 1B, histone lysine methyltransferase

function.text: SETD1B encodes histone-lysine N-methyltransferase SETD1B. Annotated molecular activities include histone H3 methyltransferase activity and histone H3K4 monomethyltransferase activity.

germline.text: Strong or definitive GenCC assertions link constitutional variants to complex neurodevelopmental disorder (autosomal dominant); intellectual developmental disorder with seizures and language delay (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Somatic sequence alterations have cohort-level candidate-driver evidence in Esophageal Adenocarcinoma; Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma; Lung Adenocarcinoma. This gene-level statistical evidence requires allele-specific review and does not establish the effect of every variant.

function.text: SETD1B encodes histone-lysine N-methyltransferase SETD1B. Based in part on similarity, it is a histone methyltransferase that catalyzes methyl group transfer from S-adenosyl-L-methionine to the epsilon-amino group of 'Lys-4' of histone H3 (H3K4) via a non-processive mechanism. It forms part of chromatin remodeling machinery, forms H3K4me1, H3K4me2 and H3K4me3 methylation marks at active chromatin sites where transcription and DNA repair take place. It contributes to regulating the transcriptional programming of multipotent hematopoietic progenitor cells and lymphoid lineage specification during hematopoiesis.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with complex neurodevelopmental disorder (autosomal dominant); intellectual developmental disorder with seizures and language delay (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving SETD1B have been reported in lung adenocarcinoma, esophageal adenocarcinoma, and pancreatic adenocarcinoma.
